title: Regional advocacy for provincial child care funding
subtitle: Howard tank repair cost increase, affordable rental housing, brownfield grants, Ontario Summer Games funding, paramedic settlement, advisory committee appointments
overview: Regional Council called on the Province of Ontario to substantially increase child care funding, citing a waitlist of over 14,000 children and a system running near full capacity. Council added wording to recognize both urban and rural centres, and the Regional Chair will send the motion to the Premier, the Education Minister, local MPs and MPPs, AMO and FCM {{vote:m12}}.

Council also approved a contract increase for the Howard water tank upgrades, after repairs turned out to be larger than first expected {{vote:m5}}. It approved priority projects for new affordable rental housing {{vote:m6}}. A committee package endorsed new Township transit services, two brownfield tax increment grants and recycling reporting requirements tied to the move to producer-run recycling {{vote:m7}}.

Council backed a $250,000 grant for the 2026 Ontario Summer Games in the region and 2026 temporary borrowing authority {{vote:m8}}. After closed session, it appointed members to the Active Transportation Advisory Committee and approved a tentative settlement with paramedics {{vote:m9}}. Council also took an update on respiratory viruses and urged vaccination.

decisions.detail: Council will press the Province for substantially more CWELCC funding, greater local flexibility and needs-based funding for the region, with the Chair communicating the motion to provincial and federal contacts and municipal associations.
Council increased the BGL Contractors Corp. contract by $888,975.22 plus taxes, for a total of $1,999,165.22, to fully repair the tank's interior coating.
Council approved the recommended priority projects under P2025-21 and authorized staff to execute the funding agreements and documents.

decisions.item: Transit, brownfield grants and recycling reporting
decisions.detail: Council endorsed a Grand River Transit application for new Township services, approved joint tax increment grants for 120 Victoria Street South and 108 Garment Street in Kitchener, and directed staff to report on landfill volumes and recycling inquiries after the 2026 transition.

decisions.item: Summer Games grant and temporary borrowing
decisions.detail: Council granted $250,000 from the Municipal Accommodation Tax reserve to Explore Waterloo Region for the 2026 Ontario Summer Games and authorized temporary borrowing in 2026.

decisions.item: Advisory committee appointments and paramedic settlement
decisions.detail: Council appointed nine members to the Active Transportation Advisory Committee and approved a tentative settlement with CUPE Local 5191 paramedic staff covering April 2024 to March 2028.

debate: On the Howard tank increase, one councillor asked why the extra work was not identified before the original tender. Staff said the interior could only be inspected by emptying the tank and taking it offline, and doing that before tendering would have kept it out of service longer.

Councillors asked how the increase would be funded and how such surprises would be avoided. Staff said it would be covered by unspent 2025 capital funds carried forward. Staff agreed to report back on funding and on tank lifecycles under the asset management plan.

During the child care motion, one councillor supported its intent but asked that the language on the Region's pressures reflect rural as well as urban centres. The mover accepted the change, and it was added without objection.

Under other business, a councillor asked how the police facility construction estimate would be tested, noting concern about a high per-square-foot figure. Staff said it is an early high-level estimate that will be refined through design and tendering, and could come in higher or lower.

Councillors also asked staff to bring back changes to the procedural by-law on correcting votes. The Clerk said such changes are tracked and expected before the October election, with no firm commitment on timing.
